rfm_tuples.R: 'Sales decreased in 2023 compared to 2022 by $412.0 million (approximately 21%) due to (i) net unfavorable market-based pricing (approximately 17%) primarily reflecting reduced ammonium sulfate pricing amid lower raw material input costs and a more stable global nitrogen fertilizer supply environment, as well as lower nylon pricing due to unfavorable supply and demand conditions and (ii) unfavorable raw material pass-through pricing (approximately 5%).' Volume change: (2.5)%. Acquisition contribution: +0.6%.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify decomposition adds up and is consistent with cash-flow direction; Mode B — derive what management did NOT say: how much of the price collapse is structural (commodity cycle reverting from 2022 spike) vs company-specific.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A Results of Operations (line ~185181) + Cash Flow Summary (line ~210559) + Q1'24 10-Q (line ~57382)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Volume (2.5)% + Pre-tax pricing (22.0)% + Acquisition +0.6% = -21.2% reconciles. Operating cash flow decreased $156.1M (-57%, $273.6M to $117.6M). Q1'24 continued the trend: sales -15.7% (volume -6.7%, price -9.0%). Self-disclosed framing correctly identifies the principal driver (ammonium sulfate price normalization post-2022 fertilizer spike). Notably, the 'increased $4.7M, or 169%' interest expense framing for a small absolute number ($7.5M) is the only conspicuous magnification — not omission.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Top-line decline is honestly attributed to commodity cycle normalization, which is verifiable cyclically (nitrogen / ammonium sulfate global pricing fell broadly in 2023 vs 2022). However the disclosure does not quantify how much of the 2022 base was a one-time fertilizer spike vs sustainable run-rate, so investors cannot triangulate the structural floor. Mode-B finding: cyclical floor disclosure gap.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In January 2024, the Company experienced a process-based operational disruption at its Frankford, Pennsylvania manufacturing site temporarily reducing phenol and acetone production at the facility, as well as production at its Hopewell and Chesterfield, Virginia facilities. As a result of a delayed ramp to targeted utilization rates, the Company recognized an unfavorable impact to pre-tax income in the first quarter 2024 of approximately $27 million ... The Company returned to targeted utilization rates at its Frankford, Pennsylvania manufacturing site, as well as across its value chain, prior to quarter end.' (Q1'24 10-Q)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the 8-K disclosure timing and the $27M magnitude; Mode B — derive whether the framing 'returned to targeted utilization rates ... prior to quarter end' is supported by the Q1 result trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1'24 10-Q (line ~56342) + 8-K filed 2024-01-19 (accession 0001673985-24-000005, 'update on plant production rates')
rfm_tuples.M_value: Jan 19 2024 8-K furnished a press release on plant production rates under Item 7.01 (Regulation FD) — timely disclosure within ~14 days of the January event. $27M Q1 pre-tax impact is the entirety of the $23.4M Q1 pre-tax loss plus more — i.e., the disruption fully explains the swing from profit to loss this quarter. Management states return to targeted rates before quarter-end. Frankford is the only U.S. phenol-from-cumene producer at scale, so this directly cascades to Hopewell (caprolactam) and Chesterfield (nylon resin) — the integrated supply chain is precisely as vulnerable as the company disclosed in risk factors.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Truthful disclosure of a material operational event with prompt 8-K, quantified Q1 impact, and a verifiable return-to-rate statement. Mode-B residual: the integrated-supply-chain vulnerability is an inherent structural risk that management discloses but does not insure against, and the $27M one-event hit on a $336M quarterly revenue base (8% of sales) shows the operational leverage cuts both ways.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the spin-off indemnification structure and any accrued environmental reserve; Mode B — derive the asymmetric tail risk from indemnifying a 70+ year operating history at Hopewell (active since 1929 as Allied Signal) without an offsetting reserve from Honeywell.

Not a 'lie' — UNVERIFIABLE by construction.

rfm_tuples.R: Critical Audit Matter (PwC): 'Quantitative Goodwill Impairment Assessment ... management changed the annual impairment assessment date to the last day of October close and performed an additional impairment assessment as of October 28, 2023. Due to the share price and current market trend, management performed a quantitative impairment assessment as of October 28, 2023 ... Management's cash flow projections for the reporting unit included significant judgments and assumptions, including revenue growth rate, EBITDA margin, and weighted average cost of capital rate.' No impairment recorded; goodwill remained $56.2M.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive what this CAM tells you about how close ASIX came to a goodwill impairment trigger, given the share-price decline and the assessment-date change mid-cycle.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Three structural facts: (1) Assessment date was CHANGED mid-year from Mar 31 to Oct 28 — an unusual mid-cycle policy revision that conveniently captures the share price downdraft window; (2) Management explicitly cites 'share price and current market trend' as the trigger for a quantitative (not qualitative) test — an admission that the qualitative screen was probably going to fail; (3) WACC and EBITDA-margin assumptions are flagged as the key sensitivities. Test result: fair value > carrying — no impairment. Cushion is not disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest CAM disclosure but the underlying narrative — mid-cycle assessment-date change + share-price-trigger quantitative test that passed — implies ASIX is close to a goodwill impairment trigger if the FY24 EBITDA-margin recovery does not materialize. The auditor implicitly signals 'we looked hard at this and it passed by some margin we won't quantify.' Mode-B priority finding.

honesty_framework_summary.verdict_rationale: Honesty framework (R/f/M) is designed to short LIARS, not bad businesses. ASIX is a cyclical chemicals issuer in a price-cycle trough with HONEST disclosure: Big-4 auditor unqualified, no covenant amendments under distress, customer concentration disclosed and stable, operational disruption disclosed timely with quantification, dividend continuity even at a loss. The 6 moderate findings are structural (cyclical floor undisclosed, tail risk unquantified) not deceptive. This is a LONG-tier name within the honesty-alpha framework: bad-looking but honestly-disclosed -36% drawdown.

summary: ASIX's FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-02-16) and Q1'24 10-Q (filed 2024-05-03) describe a cyclical chemicals issuer in a price-cycle trough with HONEST disclosure: PwC (Big 4) unqualified opinion on both financial statements and ICFR, no covenant amendments under distress (only mechanical LIBOR/SOFR + pre-scheduled step-down), no going-concern language, $30M cash + $329M revolver capacity at FY-end stepping to $20.6M + $254M at Q1'24, customer concentration stable (Shaw at 11%, top-10 at 39%, ~20-year average customer relationships, Berkshire-owned counterparty), Frankford operational disruption disclosed via timely 8-K Jan 19 2024 with quantified $27M Q1 pre-tax impact and resolution before quarter-end. Sales declined 21% in FY23 ($412M) primarily on ammonium-sulfate and nylon price normalization (-17%) with raw-material pass-through (-5%) — decomposition reconciles. Soft yellow flags: (a) three named-executive 10b5-1 plans entered in Nov-Mar window for moderate amounts with zero open-market insider buying after a -36% drawdown, (b) goodwill impairment assessment date changed mid-cycle to Oct 28 with a share-price-triggered quantitative test that PASSED (CAM), (c) dividend maintained AND raised through the trough while 2024 capex stepped up 30-40% YoY — aggressive but not opaque. The honesty framework is designed to exclude liars, not bad cyclical businesses; the framework PASSES this name. Verdict: LONG-tier — cyclical drawdown with clean disclosure quality.
